dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wonder when this war will finally be over...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Eh? Ah, it's you, citizen! Well, now that we know where those barbarians have gone, I was going to take a short rest here...

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: After all, even we legionnaires need to rest. We are not those stone folk, who know neither hunger, nor thirst, nor fatigue...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That kid over there...

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Kid? What kid? Wait... You're not talking about Tribunus Mettius, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Shh, keep your voice down, or he'll hear you! Of course, Dominus Cassiodor has said that we should not whip our soldiers, but if the Tribunus hears you, things will get ugly all the same...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: End this war?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Indeed... Alas! We've been posted here ever since those savages started large-scale border incursions. We've not seen our families for five, almost six years now.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: I wonder how Martha is doing, or if our children have grown up healthy... Moce was only two at the time. He has never even looked upon his own father...

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Still, now that Dominus Boethius is soon to arrive, this war must be soon to end... right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Be wary, citizen. Battle has been a frequent and unwelcome guest here of late.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: It's been some time since I've gotten a bulk order like this. Looks like I'll be busy...

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Oh? Hello there. Would you like to order any instruments?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you are?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: I am Giovanni, a maker of fine instruments, and the current patrono of the Pasquale family.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: My family has been making instruments for many generations. I am part of the 25th generation.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Long before the Opera Epiclese was built on Erinnyes, my ancestors were the luthiers who tuned the strings for Master Coppelius and his troupe.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: I am proud to say that over the last 500 years, at least a third of Fontaine's instruments have come from my family's workshops.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the order...

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Ah... About that. Well, I rarely receive orders from outside Fontaine, so I'm just a bit surprised, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Perhaps it's because of the Iridescence Tour's influence. Regardless, it's nothing of note.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it. Bye.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Goodbye. Remember to come and find me should you wish to place an order for any instruments.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A third? That many?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Haha, well, that might be a slight exaggeration... But no matter how you string it, we've certainly made a seventh at least!

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Though many workshops over in the Court of Fontaine have adopted mechanized production methods of late, I can guarantee you that every instrument from our workshops is 100% meticulously handcrafted. You could say this is how we uphold tradition.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: In any case, should you wish to order any instruments, simply let me know.

dialogues.speaker: Giustino
dialogues.text: Giovanni, I've already finished lacquering these instruments.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Good. I didn't think you'd still remember the craft of making instruments after all these years.

dialogues.speaker: Giustino
dialogues.text: Haha... I've utterly forgotten the complex process of crafting the peg, but the painting process? Oh, I still remember that.

dialogues.speaker: Giustino
dialogues.text: It was the most basic of basics, after all. Father scolded me countless times while I was still an apprentice. Couldn't forget it if I tried.

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: Hmph. So you do remember how instruments are made. Do you remember what makes a man, though?

dialogues.speaker: Giovanni
dialogues.text: ...Forget it. Take a break first. I'll handle the rest of the work — but watch closely, and learn well.
